text:
morgan: Heads-up — a security researcher DM'd us: a public fork of one of our example repos contains a CI build log with an AWS access key and secret that look like they map to a short-lived user used by our legacy CI runners. Treat as compromised.

rachel: ack. which repo and runner?

morgan: repo: examples/auth-samples (public fork by user `random-dev`). The log snippet points to key AKIAEXAMPLELEGACY and shows assume-role ARN: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/ci-legacy-runner-role. Looks like the runner is still using long-lived keys to assume that role.

tony: I'm owning containment. Immediate plan: 1) disable the legacy user's access keys; 2) detach the ci-legacy-runner-role from trust relationship for external tokens; 3) block the legacy runner in our CI control plane; 4) audit CloudTrail for any AssumeRole or STS:AssumeRoleWithCredentials events from the last 48h. ETA 25m.

cleo: adding steps — rotate any service principals that used that role. We should also mark the example repo as deprecated and add automated secrets scanning to our repo importers.

morgan: devops-bot — can you block CI runner group `legacy-runners` and add a WAF rule blocking requests that present that client key pattern?

devops-bot: action queued: blocking runner group `legacy-runners` in CI control plane. Updating network WAF rules to drop requests containing header X-Runner-Key: AKIAEXAMPLELEGACY.

rachel: Tony, when you disable the access keys, please paste the aws iam delete-access-key command you ran so I can reconcile in the ticket. Also, keep the keys forensics copy in the secured case folder — hashed only.

tony: Executed commands: `aws iam list-access-keys --user-name ci-legacy-user --profile prod` -> found AKIAEXAMPLELEGACY. `aws iam delete-access-key --user-name ci-legacy-user --access-key-id AKIAEXAMPLELEGACY --profile prod` -> done. I then updated the role trust policy to require `aws:CalledVia` = our-ci-service and rotated inline policies.

sec-bot: automated note: To force-expire STS tokens for a role, detach session permissions or change role trust to include an ExternalId that CI must present. Example patch applied to role trust: `"Condition": {"StringEquals": {"sts:ExternalId": "revoke-2026-10-01-01"}}`.

cleo: walk-through for audit: CloudTrail query for AssumeRole events: `aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=AssumeRole --start-time 2026-09-28T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-09-30T23:59:59Z`. Also pull VPC egress logs for IPs matching runner traffic.

morgan: I've opened incidentINC-2026-441 and flagged priority P1 until audit complete. Rachel, get legal on the thread if external actor used the creds.

rachel: contacting legal and compliance now. Also notifying product owners of potentially impacted customers (none expected since it was a legacy example runner bound to staging).

tony: scanning found 3 AssumeRole calls from last 36h from two IPs: 35.198.23.14 and 18.197.101.5. Those map to CI runner infra. No calls to prod services observed, only to staging accounts.

cleo: follow-up actions we should track:
- Remove all long-lived keys for CI users and move to OIDC-based role assumption
- Add pre-commit hook and CI check to scan for AWS secret patterns and fail builds on detection
- One-off secret scrub for history (git filter-repo) on any internal forks that contain keys
- Create migration plan for legacy runners -> scheduled sprint ticket

morgan: agree. Tony / Cleo, add remediation PRs and schedule a triage meeting. Also add a short notice to infra@ and support@ that staging CI was degraded for ~15m while we rotated keys.

rachel: legal replied — they want the forensics bundle and confirmation no customer data was accessed. Tony, package CloudTrail extract and put in secure case.

tony: CloudTrail export completed and uploaded to secure-case/INC-2026-441/artifacts (link shared in private ticket). Found no S3 GetObject or DynamoDB access outside CI orchestration.

morgan: closing interim response here: containment complete, keys revoked, runner blocked, audit in progress. Reopen thread if new evidence appears. Thanks all. :lock:
